rules.name: slop: listicles and prompt packs
rules.note: Deliberately before the keep rule: a listicle about Claude is still a listicle.
rules.query: ^(the )?(top|best) ?[0-9]+ .*(tools|apps|prompts|extensions|websites|plugins|hacks|tricks)\b|^[0-9]+ (best|top|amazing|mind-blowing|must-try) .*(tools|apps|prompts|websites|extensions)\b|^[0-9]+ (chatgpt|ai|claude|gemini) prompts\b|\bultimate guide to\b|\bmake money with\b|\b10x your\b

rules.name: slop: sponsored and giveaways
rules.note: Paid placement and course funnels. Also before the keep rule — a sponsored post about OpenAI is an ad.
rules.query: \b(sponsored|advertorial|promoted post|paid partnership|giveaway|free course|enroll now|masterclass|limited seats|discount code|coupon)\b|\[sponsored\]

rules.name: keep: labs, models and papers
rules.note: The shield. Rules are first-match-wins, so everything below this line is forbidden from touching an article that names a lab, a model or an arXiv paper — it goes to the model with its summary and entities intact. Widen this before widening anything else.

rules.name: noise: crypto and web3
rules.note: An AI x crypto piece that names a lab is already protected by the keep rule above.

rules.name: noise: ticker moves
rules.note: Share-price coverage, not company news. Written narrowly on purpose: a bare \"shares\" would archive \"OpenAI shares new details\", and funding rounds must stay — they are a category of their own.

rules.name: noise: deals and shopping
rules.query: \b([0-9]{1,3}% off|black friday|cyber monday|prime day|best deals?|deal of the (day|week)|on sale now|save \$[0-9]+|lowest price ever)\b

rules.name: noise: podcasts and video
rules.note: There is no text to read, so there is no note to write.

rules.name: noise: hiring posts
rules.query: \b(is hiring|we're hiring|we are hiring|now hiring|job openings?|apply now|join our team)\b|\(yc [swf][0-9]{2}\)

rules.name: noise: HN meta threads
rules.note: Ask HN and Tell HN are discussion, not news. Show HN is left alone on purpose — that is where the tools show up.

rules.name: noise: press-release wires
rules.note: Off by default: mostly marketing, but a real launch sometimes only exists on the wire. Run `giznews rules test --rule \"noise: press-release wires\"` against your own archive before switching it on.

rules.name: noise: weekly roundups
rules.note: Off by default: this is what giznews digest already does — but if you subscribe to a weekly AI newsletter on purpose, this rule kills the source you chose.
rules.query: \b(week in review|this week in (ai|tech|machine learning)|weekly (roundup|digest|recap|newsletter)|news roundup|link roundup|what we'?re reading|issue #[0-9]+)\b

rules.name: noise: consumer gadgets
rules.note: Off by default: \"Apple brings AI to the iPhone\" is real news and this rule would archive it. Only switch it on if your feed carries a general-tech source.

rules.name: noise: clickbait
rules.note: Only phrases no real headline uses. \"Slams\" and \"fires back\" are deliberately absent: regulators slam companies, and that is regulation news.
rules.query: \b(goes viral|you won'?t believe|will blow your mind|shocking truth|breaks the internet|claps back|throws shade|what happened next)\b
